mapping.col3: CICS transaction entry point → Spring Boot startup; MQ infrastructure replaced by embedded Tomcat HTTP server
MQOPEN for input queue → Spring registers POST /api/accounts/enquiry at startup; no runtime open needed
MQOPEN for reply queue → HTTP response; Spring manages all I/O lifecycle automatically
MQOPEN for CARD.DEMO.ERROR → @RestControllerAdvice; errors become HTTP 400/500 instead of MQ messages
PERFORM UNTIL NO-MORE-MSGS loop → stateless REST: each HTTP request is an independent invocation
MQGET (5-second wait) → Spring deserialises JSON request body; correlation ID echoed via synchronous HTTP
EXEC CICS READ DATASET(\'ACCTDAT\') → accountRepository.findById(); EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD → Optional.isEmpty()
MQPUT to CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT → HTTP 200 JSON body; SAVE-CORELID echoed automatically by HTTP
MQPUT error to CARD.DEMO.ERROR → HTTP 500 with JSON error body; logged via SLF4J
EXEC CICS RETURN → method return; MQCLOSE operations managed by Spring container lifecycle
MQCLOSE for input queue → no Java equivalent; Spring Data JPA connections managed by HikariCP pool
MQCLOSE for reply queue → no Java equivalent; HTTP response is sent and connection closed by servlet container
MQCLOSE for error queue → no Java equivalent; exception handler is stateless, fires per-request

package com.carddemo.account.web.dto; import java.math.BigDecimal; /** * Replaces the WS-ACCT-RESPONSE working-storage area in COACCT01.cbl. * *

The COBOL program formatted all fields into a 1000-byte text buffer * (REPLY-MESSAGE) that was placed on the MQ reply queue. This DTO * replaces that with a structured JSON response. * *

When the account is found ({@code DFHRESP(NORMAL)}), {@code error} is null * and all account fields are populated. * When the account is not found ({@code DFHRESP(NOTFND)}) or the request is * invalid, only {@code error} is set. * * @param accountId ACCT-ID PIC 9(11) * @param activeStatus ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS PIC X(01) — 'Y' or 'N' * @param currentBalance ACCT-CURR-BAL PIC S9(10)V99 * @param creditLimit ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT PIC S9(10)V99 * @param cashCreditLimit ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT PIC S9(10)V99 * @param openDate ACCT-OPEN-DATE PIC X(10) — YYYY-MM-DD * @param expirationDate ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE (sic) PIC X(10) — YYYY-MM-DD * @param reissueDate ACCT-REISSUE-DATE PIC X(10) — YYYY-MM-DD * @param currCycCredit ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT PIC S9(10)V99 * @param currCycDebit ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT PIC S9(10)V99 * @param groupId ACCT-GROUP-ID PIC X(10) * @param error null on success; error description on failure */ public record AccountEnquiryResponse( Long accountId, String activeStatus, BigDecimal currentBalance, BigDecimal creditLimit, BigDecimal cashCreditLimit, String openDate, String expirationDate, String reissueDate, BigDecimal currCycCredit, BigDecimal currCycDebit, String groupId, String error ) { /** Successful response — account found. */ public static AccountEnquiryResponse success( Long accountId, String activeStatus, BigDecimal currentBalance, BigDecimal creditLimit, BigDecimal cashCreditLimit, String openDate, String expirationDate, String reissueDate, BigDecimal currCycCredit, BigDecimal currCycDebit, String groupId) { return new AccountEnquiryResponse( accountId, activeStatus, currentBalance, creditLimit, cashCreditLimit, openDate, expirationDate, reissueDate, currCycCredit, currCycDebit, groupId, null); } /** * Error response — mirrors the COBOL STRING … INTO REPLY-MESSAGE pattern * used for DFHRESP(NOTFND) and invalid-request cases. */ public static AccountEnquiryResponse error(String message) { return new AccountEnquiryResponse( null, null, null, null, null, null, null, null, null, null, null, message); } }

ACCOUNT-RECORD.b: Full account record layout from copybook CVACT01Y — 300-byte VSAM KSDS record

ACCT-ID.b: Account number — 11-digit unique credit-card account identifier (primary key)

ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS.b: Account active flag — PIC X(01), Y=active N=inactive

ACCT-CURR-BAL.b: Current account balance — PIC S9(10)V99 COMP-3

ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT.b: Maximum credit limit for purchases — PIC S9(10)V99

ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT.b: Maximum credit limit for cash advances — PIC S9(10)V99

ACCT-OPEN-DATE.b: Date the account was opened — PIC X(10) format YYYY-MM-DD

ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE.b: Card expiration date — PIC X(10) YYYY-MM-DD (note: EXPIRAION typo retained from source)

ACCT-REISSUE-DATE.b: Date the card was last reissued — PIC X(10) YYYY-MM-DD

ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT.b: Total credits applied in the current billing cycle — PIC S9(10)V99

ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT.b: Total debits applied in the current billing cycle — PIC S9(10)V99

ACCT-GROUP-ID.b: Portfolio or product group identifier — PIC X(10)

WS-ACCT-RESPONSE.b: Working-storage response area — 1000-byte text buffer formatted for MQ reply
WS-ACCT-RESPONSE.j: AccountEnquiryResponse record — JSON response DTO replacing the text buffer

WS-ACCT-ID.b: Account ID copied into response area from ACCT-ID after successful CICS READ

WS-ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS.b: Active status copied into response area from ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS

WS-ACCT-CURR-BAL.b: Current balance copied into response area from ACCT-CURR-BAL

WS-ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT.b: Credit limit copied into response area from ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT

WS-ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT.b: Cash credit limit copied into response area from ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT

WS-ACCT-OPEN-DATE.b: Open date copied into response area from ACCT-OPEN-DATE

WS-ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE.b: Expiration date copied into response area from ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE

WS-ACCT-REISSUE-DATE.b: Reissue date copied into response area from ACCT-REISSUE-DATE

WS-ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT.b: Cycle credit copied into response area from ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT

WS-ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT.b: Cycle debit copied into response area from ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT

WS-ACCT-GROUP-ID.b: Group ID copied into response area from ACCT-GROUP-ID

REQUEST-MSG-COPY.b: Structured overlay of MQ-BUFFER — WS-FUNC (4 bytes) + WS-KEY (11 digits) + WS-FILLER
REQUEST-MSG-COPY.j: AccountEnquiryRequest record — JSON deserialised from HTTP POST body

WS-FUNC.b: Function code — PIC X(04); must be INQA for account enquiry

WS-KEY.b: Account key — PIC 9(11); the ACCT-ID to look up

WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID.b: Account ID formatted as numeric RIDFLD for EXEC CICS READ — PIC 9(11)

WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X.b: Character REDEFINES of WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID — PIC X(11); used as RIDFLD string for CICS READ
WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X.j: No Java equivalent — accountRepository.findById(Long) accepts numeric key directly

WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM.b: Card number field in RIDFLD group — PIC X(16); unused in the account-enquiry path
WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM.j: No Java equivalent — card number lookup not part of this service

WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID.b: Customer ID in RIDFLD group — PIC 9(09); unused in the account-enquiry path
WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID.j: No Java equivalent — customer lookup not part of this service

WS-RESP-CD.b: CICS EXEC response code — DFHRESP(NORMAL) = 0, DFHRESP(NOTFND) = 13
WS-RESP-CD.j: No Java equivalent — Optional.isEmpty() replaces EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD

WS-REAS-CD.b: CICS EXEC response reason code — supplementary diagnostic from RESP2
WS-REAS-CD.j: No Java equivalent — Spring Data exceptions carry diagnostic info via getMessage()

WS-CICS-RESP1-CD.b: CICS RESP from EXEC CICS RETRIEVE — checks that the trigger start succeeded
WS-CICS-RESP1-CD.j: No Java equivalent — REST endpoint is always available; no CICS trigger mechanism

WS-CICS-RESP2-CD.b: CICS RESP2 supplementary code from EXEC CICS RETRIEVE
WS-CICS-RESP2-CD.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP 400/500 status codes replace RESP2 diagnostics

LIT-ACCTFILENAME.b: VSAM DDNAME literal — PIC X(8) VALUE ACCTDAT; used in EXEC CICS READ DATASET()
LIT-ACCTFILENAME.j: @Table(name="accounts") on Account entity — database table name replaces DDNAME

MQ-BUFFER.b: 1000-byte raw MQ message payload — received by MQGET and sent by MQPUT
MQ-BUFFER.j: No Java equivalent — Jackson automatically serialises/deserialises JSON; no explicit buffer

MQ-BUFFER-LENGTH.b: Length of MQ-BUFFER passed to MQGET/MQPUT calls — fixed at 1000
MQ-BUFFER-LENGTH.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP Content-Length handled by servlet container

MQ-CONDITION-CODE.b: MQ API completion code — MQCC-OK=0, MQCC-FAILED=2; checked after every MQ call
MQ-CONDITION-CODE.j: No Java equivalent — Spring throws exceptions on failure; checked via try/catch

MQ-REASON-CODE.b: MQ API reason code — MQRC-NO-MSG-AVAILABLE=2033 signals empty queue
MQ-REASON-CODE.j: No Java equivalent — empty result represented by Optional.empty() from findById()

MQ-HCONN.b: MQ queue manager connection handle — returned by MQCONN, passed to all MQ calls
MQ-HCONN.j: No Java equivalent — JPA EntityManager/HikariCP manage database connections

MQ-HOBJ.b: MQ queue object handle — returned by MQOPEN, passed to MQGET/MQPUT/MQCLOSE
MQ-HOBJ.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP socket managed by embedded Tomcat

MQ-OPTIONS.b: Bitfield of MQ open options — MQOO-INPUT-SHARED, MQOO-OUTPUT, MQOO-FAIL-IF-QUIESCING
MQ-OPTIONS.j: No Java equivalent — REST endpoint options declared in annotations

MQ-CORRELID.b: MQ message correlation ID — 24-byte binary; echoed from request to reply for routing
MQ-CORRELID.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP is synchronous; client correlation implicit in TCP connection

MQ-MSG-ID.b: MQ message ID — 24-byte unique message identifier assigned by queue manager
MQ-MSG-ID.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP uses TCP session for message identity

MQ-MSG-COUNT.b: Counter of messages processed in this CICS activation — PIC 9(09)
MQ-MSG-COUNT.j: No Java equivalent — REST is stateless; metrics collected externally via Micrometer

SAVE-CORELID.b: Saved correlation ID from inbound message — used to correlate MQPUT reply
SAVE-CORELID.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP correlation is implicit in the synchronous request/response

SAVE-MSGID.b: Saved message ID from inbound message — echoed in MQMD-MSGID of reply
SAVE-MSGID.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP does not require message ID echoing

SAVE-REPLY2Q.b: Saved reply-to queue name from MQMD-REPLYTOQ — target for MQPUT reply
SAVE-REPLY2Q.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP response goes back to the same TCP connection

QUEUE-INFO.b: Queue configuration group — QMGR-NAME, INPUT-QUEUE-NAME, REPLY-QUEUE-NAME, ERROR-QUEUE-NAME
QUEUE-INFO.j: No Java equivalent — endpoint URL and exception handling replace queue configuration

QMGR-NAME.b: IBM MQ queue manager name — identifies the MQ broker
QMGR-NAME.j: No Java equivalent — database URL in application.yml replaces MQ broker configuration

INPUT-QUEUE-NAME.b: MQ input queue name — read from CICS trigger, e.g. CARD.DEMO.ACCT.INQUEUE
INPUT-QUEUE-NAME.j: No Java equivalent — POST /api/accounts/enquiry is the fixed endpoint URL

REPLY-QUEUE-NAME.b: MQ reply queue — hardcoded as CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT for account enquiry replies
REPLY-QUEUE-NAME.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP response goes back to the requesting client directly

ERROR-QUEUE-NAME.b: MQ error queue — hardcoded as CARD.DEMO.ERROR for error message routing
ERROR-QUEUE-NAME.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP 500 replaces error queue; logs go to stdout/SLF4J

INPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE.b: Object handle for the open input queue — passed to MQGET calls
INPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP socket managed by embedded Tomcat

OUTPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE.b: Object handle for the open output (reply) queue — passed to MQPUT calls
OUTPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP response stream managed by servlet container

ERROR-QUEUE-HANDLE.b: Object handle for the open error queue — passed to MQPUT error calls
ERROR-QUEUE-HANDLE.j: No Java equivalent — GlobalExceptionHandler writes errors to HTTP response

QMGR-HANDLE-CONN.b: Queue manager connection handle — returned by MQCONN, passed to MQOPEN/MQCLOSE
QMGR-HANDLE-CONN.j: No Java equivalent — database connection pool managed by Spring/HikariCP

REPLY-MESSAGE.b: 1000-byte text buffer for the formatted reply placed on the MQ reply queue
REPLY-MESSAGE.j: AccountEnquiryResponse record — structured JSON replaces the flat text buffer

REQUEST-MESSAGE.b: Intermediate buffer — copy of MQ-BUFFER used to parse the incoming request
REQUEST-MESSAGE.j: No Java equivalent — Jackson directly deserialises HTTP body into AccountEnquiryRequest

ERROR-MESSAGE.b: 1000-byte error text buffer — copy of MQ-ERR-DISPLAY sent to error queue
ERROR-MESSAGE.j: No Java equivalent — exception message propagated via HTTP 500 response body

QUEUE-MESSAGE.b: Raw 1000-byte message workspace before structured parsing
QUEUE-MESSAGE.j: No Java equivalent — raw HTTP body bytes handled transparently by Spring MVC

WS-MQ-MSG-FLAG.b: MQ message exhausted flag — PIC X(01); set to Y when MQRC-NO-MSG-AVAILABLE
WS-MQ-MSG-FLAG.j: No Java equivalent — REST is stateless; Optional.empty() signals not-found

NO-MORE-MSGS.b: 88-level condition on WS-MQ-MSG-FLAG = Y — terminates the PERFORM UNTIL loop
NO-MORE-MSGS.j: No Java equivalent — REST processes one request per HTTP call; no loop needed

WS-RESP-QUEUE-STS.b: Reply queue open status flag — PIC X(01); Y after successful MQOPEN
WS-RESP-QUEUE-STS.j: No Java equivalent — Spring Boot endpoint is always ready; no manual open state

RESP-QUEUE-OPEN.b: 88-level condition on WS-RESP-QUEUE-STS = Y — guards MQCLOSE in 8000-TERMINATION
RESP-QUEUE-OPEN.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP output channel managed by servlet container

WS-ERR-QUEUE-STS.b: Error queue open status flag — PIC X(01); Y after successful MQOPEN on error queue
WS-ERR-QUEUE-STS.j: No Java equivalent — GlobalExceptionHandler is always active; no open state

ERR-QUEUE-OPEN.j: No Java equivalent — exception handler active for lifetime of application

WS-REPLY-QUEUE-STS.b: Reply queue open status flag — separate from WS-RESP-QUEUE-STS; guards MQCLOSE
WS-REPLY-QUEUE-STS.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP lifecycle managed by container

REPLY-QUEUE-OPEN.j: No Java equivalent — REST response channel is always available

WS-DATE-TIME.b: Date/time working storage group — ABS-TIME (binary) + formatted MMDDYYYY + TIME
WS-DATE-TIME.j: No Java equivalent — date/time not used in the Java account-enquiry service

WS-ABS-TIME.b: CICS absolute time — PIC S9(15) COMP-3; used as timestamp base
WS-ABS-TIME.j: No Java equivalent — Java LocalDateTime / Instant used if timestamping needed

MQ-ERR-DISPLAY.b: Formatted error display record — paragraph name + return message + codes + queue name
MQ-ERR-DISPLAY.j: No Java equivalent — exception stack trace and message served via HTTP 500 JSON body

MQ-ERROR-PARA.b: Name of the paragraph that triggered the error — PIC X(25)
MQ-ERROR-PARA.j: No Java equivalent — stack trace in exception identifies the failing method

MQ-APPL-RETURN-MESSAGE.b: Human-readable error description — PIC X(25); e.g. INP MQGET ERR
MQ-APPL-RETURN-MESSAGE.j: No Java equivalent — exception getMessage() provides the error description

MQ-APPL-CONDITION-CODE.b: MQ completion code formatted for display — PIC 9(02)
MQ-APPL-CONDITION-CODE.j: No Java equivalent — HTTP status code (400/500) replaces MQ condition codes

MQ-APPL-REASON-CODE.b: MQ reason code formatted for display — PIC 9(05)
MQ-APPL-REASON-CODE.j: No Java equivalent — exception type and message replace MQ reason codes

MQ-APPL-QUEUE-NAME.b: Queue name formatted for error display — PIC X(48)
MQ-APPL-QUEUE-NAME.j: No Java equivalent — endpoint URL context included in Spring error logging
